differential_evidence.description: ESR and CRP levels — markedly elevated ESR/CRP strongly supports PMR (and may be elevated in inflammatory myopathy), whereas adhesive capsulitis/rotator-cuff disease typically has normal systemic inflammatory markers.
Serum creatine kinase (CK) — significantly elevated CK supports an inflammatory myopathy (polymyositis); CK is usually normal in PMR and in adhesive capsulitis.

Shoulder exam: passive versus active range of motion — loss of both active and passive ROM (particularly external rotation) points to adhesive capsulitis; preserved passive ROM with reduced active ROM (pain-limited) suggests rotator-cuff tear or pain-limited movement seen in PMR.

Short trial of low-dose prednisone (and time to improvement) — rapid dramatic symptom improvement within days favors PMR; lack of rapid response (or need for higher-dose/longer therapy) makes PMR less likely and raises concern for inflammatory myopathy or structural shoulder disease.
